notes.title: HOTFIX | #001 Game Update
notes.content:
Hello, Boss!

We’d like to share details of our first hotfix and some key gameplay updates.

[h1]Gameplay Updates[/h1]

[list]
[*] Random Starting Squad in Campaign Mode - We've updated the campaign so that each new playthrough begins with a different starting squad. Previously, the squad was fixed to deliver the tutorial experience as intended by the dev team. However, based on player feedback, we've decided to introduce more variety. (PMC-0853)
[*] No Excessively Negative Modifiers in Campaign Starters - Operators with extreme negative modifiers will no longer appear in the starting squad for campaign mode. These traits were unintentionally raising the difficulty level for new players. This change ensures a smoother onboarding experience. (PMC-0856)
[*] Improved Late-Game Level Design in Freeplay - We’ve adjusted the difficulty curve in the later stages of Freeplay. Previously, some players reported hitting a wall due to overly punishing and inconsistent difficulty spikes. We aim to make Freeplay more accessible while planning to reintroduce higher difficulty through optional modifiers in future updates. (PMC-0861)
[/list]

[h1]Other Gameplay Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] UI Update to Bring More Focus to the Freeplay - We've made UI adjustments across the build to better spotlight Freeplay mode. (PMC-0862)
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] In-Game: Fixed a crash caused by grenade throws. (PMC-0846)
[*] In-Game: Fixed an issue where grenades couldn’t be thrown when certain gun mods were equipped. (PMC-0857)
[*] In-Game: Fixed a bug where headshot damage was missing from post-mission stats. (PMC-0863)
[*] Freeplay: Fixed a bug that prevented returning to the main menu. (PMC-0848)
[*] Freeplay: Fixed a crash when opening the armory without any gear equipped. (PMC-0867)
[*] Campaign: Fixed an issue where operators' gear would disappear if they were not re-contracted. (PMC-0844)
[*] Missions: Fixed a bug where the same operator could appear twice in an event. (PMC-0715)
[*] UI: Fixed improper scaling on multi-monitor setups with various DPI and resolution settings. (PMC-0866)
[/list]

We’re incredibly grateful for the enthusiasm you've shown toward Private Military Manager. We're committed to quickly improving the gameplay experience and expanding content based on your feedback. Don’t hesitate to share your thoughts with us in the community—your input is invaluable.

Thank you!

notes.title: Update | A completely revamped demo!
notes.content:
Hello, Boss.

Since the demo launch on January 20th, a whopping 30,343 bosses have experienced Private Military Manager. 🎉

After that, we have been racing toward the Early Access release on April 28th, and couldn’t update the demo as much as we wanted.

Now, we've fully updated the demo to align with the Early Access version's content framework, including:

[list]
[*]Expanded narrative in Story Mode
[*]More diverse weapon combinations
[*]A vast skill tree
[*]Finely tuned balance
[/list]

Free Play mode is temporarily unavailable for now, but rest assured — it's packed with much richer content than the previous demo.

Enjoy, and see you in Private Military Manager: Tactical Auto Battler!

notes.title: Coming soon! Early Access for Private Military Manager begins on April 28.
notes.content:
Hello, Boss.

Finally! At last! Private Military Manager is launching in Early Access! 🎉

The launch date and time is April 27th at 11:59 PM. (PDT)

Here’s what has been improved compared to the demo version:

The story, which previously only covered the prologue, has been expanded up to the mid-point.
- Unique mercenaries will now join the player on their journey.
- In Free Play mode, balance adjustments now create a clearer need for generational shifts among mercenaries.
- The tech tree linked to company growth has been significantly revised.

And here's what we have planned for the period between Early Access and the official release:
- Completion of the story.
- Addition of mission modifiers to encourage more strategic decision-making.
- Enhanced influence of faction relationships.
- More dramatic narrative developments based on faction relationships and mission progress.
- More fleshed-out mercenary characters that react more naturally to various situations.
- A system where interpersonal relationships between mercenaries affect their individual behaviors.
- A progression system for the manager.
- A company growth system.
- A system for farming items and parts.

Private Military Manager is constantly evolving! We hope you’ll continue to look forward to what’s coming.

We can’t wait to see you turn our unruly band of mercs into a top-tier outfit!

We monitor the Steam Community Hub daily, so if you have any feedback, feel free to drop by and share it with us.

Thank you so much for waiting!

notes.title: DEV LOG | #1 Training Schedule Rework
notes.content:
Hello, boss.

What did you think about the mercenary training system while playing Private Military Manager? The PMM game designer described the decision-making depth of the current training system as "a level of decision-making that can be done with just three lines of Python code." One thing is clear: the current training system does not align with the development direction of PMM. We expect each of our decisions to be impactful and deep when playing PMM.

[previewyoutube=NyqM1dsI0CQ;full][/previewyoutube]

Since the prologue was released on September 9th, the PMM development team has been reworking the mercenary training system.

The planning intentions are as follows:
[list]
[*] Reduce the number and frequency of choices while enhancing the depth and fun of each choice.
[*] Provide a sense of achievement through the experience of optimizing growth and stability within various constraints.
[*] Enhance details so that mercenaries feel more human and give a better sense of managing those people.
[*] Allow the choice to be a moral manager leading mercenaries well or an evil manager treating them as expendables.
[/list]

[previewyoutube=REW7UR0GZ6s;full][/previewyoutube]

As a result, we are testing features that reflect the following elements:
[list]
[*] Divide the day into three segments and decide which training ground each mercenary will spend each segment. You can decide what training and rest to instruct for each segment.
[*] You must find the optimal combination among the possible two-digit combinations for each training ground, considering various factors such as traits and synergy between mercenaries.
[*] Instead of a critical injury occurring immediately, a minor injury occurs as a sign, and responding well to this can prevent a major injury. On the other hand, you can also push them into training with painkillers to pass immediate evaluations or promises.
[/list]

Currently, we are in the stage of testing functionality, so UI design is not considered at all, and it is in a simple state where only the game experience can be observed. However, the development team is very satisfied with the current functionality and feels that the game is progressing.

After the rework of the training schedule, there are plans to develop a tech tree feature to advance the company itself and improve events to make each mercenary feel more human and strengthen the player's role as a leader.

Additionally, a demo is scheduled to be released in December, and we will come to you with a free mode with greatly enhanced replayability.

We will also inform you soon about participating in G-STAR.

Instead of a critical injury occurring immediately, a minor injury occurs as a sign, and responding well to this can prevent a major injury. On the other hand, you can also push them into training with painkillers to pass immediate evaluations or promises.

notes.title: Playtest Build Update #5
notes.content:
Hello, this is the Private Military Manger development team.

[h1]Development Progress[/h1]

During playtesting, we've noticed that playtesters are quitting the game early on more often than we expected. We're trying to figure out what issues are keeping players from staying interested in the gameplay and how we can improve our early game onboarding.
We need your feedback! Let us know what difficulties you've encountered while playing the game via the Google Form, the Steam Community, or by commenting on this post.

[url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd-LVs8TxPeKEDUcEzzum2MjzkLCSDgr2L39mXiPWMb8Cv8cw/viewform?usp=sf_link]Survey page[/url]

Here are the major changes in this update.

[list]
[*] Onboarding: We've improved the flow of gameplay so that players new to the game can see in-game scenes more early.
[*] Help System: We've added a help system: Instead of players learning gameplay through character dialog, we've modified the help system so that players can learn the information they need to play the game.
[*] Other improvements: Improved the equipment window UI; Removed some unnecessary pop-up UI; Updated some cutscenes to be skippable.
[/list]

Thanks.

notes.title: Playtest Build Update #4
notes.content:
Hello! This is the Private Military Manager development team.
[h1]Automation Games Sale 2024[/h1]
Private Military Manager participated in the Automation Games Sale 2024! It was a great opportunity to meet many players, which has been very beneficial for both our team and the game. We believe many of you may have seen our game featured on the store page. We are currently exploring various ways to further expose and promote our game.

[h1]Development Progress[/h1]
As mentioned previously, we are preparing a public demo. We are considering how to structure the demo so that players who try it out will be excited about the game. Additionally, we are constantly thinking about what gameplay fans of the genre expect and what improvements are needed to deliver the gameplay experience they anticipate. Here are the major changes in this update.

[list]
[*] Content and Level Design: We have increased the volume of encounter and quest content, and improved some level designs. We've tried to reduce the occurrence of unreasonable and unattainable quests, but there may still be occasional issues that we will continue to address.
[*] Challenge Mode: We have added an experimental Challenge Mode: Survive as long as possible while facing increasingly tougher threats and solving various problems each week!
[*] UI Improvements and Presentation: We have reworked some UIs, such as the operation planning screen, to make the game look more visually appealing! We are also steadily adding more animation and other presentation elements to the game.
[*] In-Game Presentation: Added new cinematic elements to real combat: in the first mission, a building explodes.
[*] And as always, various bug fixes and performance improvements: Improved the sluggish mouse response issue in the out-game interface. We are continuously working on enhancing the overall performance and responsiveness of the game.
[/list]

Known Issues
[list]
[*] Mercenary list not visible when loading a game: Reloading the game in the settings will resolve this issue.
[/list]

Thank you!

notes.title: Playtest Build Update #3
notes.content:
Hello, this is the Private Military Manager development team.

[h1]Development Progress[/h1]

We are preparing a public demo build: We're hoping to have a demo build ready for the next steam nextfest, and hope to have it ready before then so that more players can try it out. Many of you have given us feedback, but we still have a lot of work to do in terms of UI and usability, presentation of information, and accessibility and convenience of the information players need to perform management tasks. Localization and translation are also still very immature.

We'll continue to playtest and update our development builds before the public demo.

Here are the changes in this update.

[list]
[*] Clean up in-game overlays: We were left with a legacy of non-localized overlays in-game, which often caused functionality errors. We moved most of the functionality of the legacy overlays to new overlays and cleaned up the in-game HUD!
[*] Quests: formerly known as "quests" or "commitments" within the development team. Mercenaries will no longer sit still and do what they're told, then suddenly start fighting and whining about it. They'll now request improvements based on their view of mission readiness, and whine about it if they don't get them. If you promise to do what they ask, they'll be happy, but you'll have to carefully schedule and choose your event options to keep that promise. It's up to you to be a respectable boss who keeps his promises, or an irresponsible boss who yells, "Do you all live by your promises?"
[*] Other UI polish and improvements
[/list]

Thank you!

notes.title: Playtest Build Update #2
notes.content:
Hello, this is the Private Military Manager development team.

We've updated the playtest build once more.

[h1]How is the playtest going?[/h1]
As much as we'd love to release the game once we've polished the gameplay to a level we're happy with, this isn't always the best option in the real world. It's a necessary part of making a game to see if the concepts and gameplay experiences we envision and create are interesting to a large number of players, and to get feedback to improve the game, which is what we're doing with Steam Playtesting.

Each week we're making improvements to areas of the game that we feel are undercooked and underdeveloped, and we're seeing how our playtesters feel about the improvements. As any development team will tell you, your feedback is incredibly helpful!

Here are the changes in this update.

[list]
[*] Performance improvements, in-game speed settings: We've generally improved the performance of in-game gameplay - we're hoping to see 30 frames in most environments where 3D games are playable. Along with the performance improvements, we've added in-game speed settings: You can fast-forward in-game to check the results quickly!
[*] In-game interactivity: Players are now able to choose where to throw grenades in-game. Squad members can be reordered in-game.
[*] UI improvements: New UIs are being added all the time: The following UIs have been updated: Squad List (Loadout), Shop, and Armory.
[*] Level Design: We've polished the level design to make gameplay more interesting and challenging.
[*] More equipment: We've made the equipment listed in the store more diverse. Along with the price of hiring and retaining mercenaries, we hope to make you think more about resource utilization during gameplay.
[/list]

Thank you!

notes.title: Playtest Build Update #1
notes.content:
Playtest Build Update #1

Hello, this is the Private Military Manager development team.

We've updated the playtest build and given more people access to play the build.
It would be very helpful if you could play the build and leave us some feedback!

[list]
[*] [url=https://forms.gle/pfLSZgZivDj2US7G6]Survey page[/url]
[*] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2564320/discussions/]Steam Community[/url]
[/list]

[h1]What's Changed?[/h1]

In the previous announcement, you can see what we've been spending our time on.
For those of you who have been playing the playtest build, here are the major gameplay changes.

[list]
[*] Weekly Goals: In previous builds, it was difficult for players to tell if they were making the right decisions in the game, or if they were on track with their company and in-game strategy, or if they were having trouble and unable to complete missions. To improve this, players are given weekly goals: If a player doesn't meet enough of their weekly goals, their "Trust" level goes down, and if their "Trust" level goes down enough, they fail the mission. We hope this will help players recognize when they're having trouble and retry the game more quickly.
[*] More complex character creation: We've added more modifiers to characters. Modifiers can have a variety of effects on a mercenary's personality, as well as on other mercenaries and the state of the company as a whole. We hope you'll consider modifiers carefully when hiring new mercenaries, and that they can intertwine to create unexpected challenges for players.
[*] In-game interactions: We are implementing a feature that will allow players to manually perform some in-game actions that were previously performed automatically, such as throwing grenades and using medkits. We currently have the first prototype of this feature in a build. We hope this will allow players to be more observant in-game and feel like they can make better choices than the AI to solve in-game problems.
[*] UI: We're redesigning the entire game's UI again: Currently, the UI looks inconsistent with a mix of pre-renewal and post-renewal UI, and we aim to have a consistent and more usable UI as soon as possible.
[/list]

Below are other changes.
[list]
[*] Player Name: When you start a game, you can now name your player!
[*] Experience: Mercenaries can now earn experience through trials and real-world battles.
[*] and many other bug fixes
[/list]

Thank you!

notes.title: Playtesting, Game Experience
notes.content:
Hello, this is the Private Military Manager development team.

[h1]Playtesting, Game Experience[/h1]

It's been two weeks since we've shared any news. We've been so busy making the game that we haven't been able to share updates as often as we'd like. We've had more people sign up for the playtest than we ever thought possible. Thank you to everyone who signed up.

Now that we've cleaned up the build, we're ready to start playtesting. Before we get to the playtest, we wanted to give you a quick overview of what kind of game we're making, what kind of experience we wanted to give you with this build, and what we have planned for the future.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
In Private Military Manager, you play as the owner of a mercenary company and you have to run the company and complete your missions. The game is divided into two main parts: the combat part (core gameplay) and the operations part (loop gameplay).

The core gameplay consists of loadouts, mission planning, and combat. In combat, the player sees how the mercenaries participate and contribute to the battle. They must imagine how they can change their loadouts and operational plans to meet the challenges presented to them, and refine them to help their mercenaries perform better in combat and, as a result, complete the mission. Depending on the situation and environment of the mission, you'll need to decide which role you want to deploy your mercenaries in (we currently have five roles), how you want to equip each mercenary, and how you want to utilize their abilities and resources. The experience of successfully completing a mission is a rewarding one, as you struggle to solve the mission and solve the problems that arise while preparing for it.

Combat is an important part of the game, but running your company and preparing your squad to perform well in combat is just as important: You'll need to decide which mercenaries to recruit and how to train and develop them. Mercenaries can be developed through daily training, and perks can be used to make them more effective in specific situations. We want players to think about how to invest their limited resources, including cash and credit, to complete missions.

Over the course of a mission, players will encounter a variety of events and make a series of choices, some of which will help them run their company and advance the mission, but many of which will present new management and operational issues and challenges for players to solve. Just like in real life, unexpected issues may arise just before a mission, or your squad may not build up in the way you initially envisioned. We hope you'll find it exciting and challenging to control or deal with the risks and uncertainties as you complete the mission.

You can familiarize yourself with the game and learn the basic rules of gameplay through the Scenario Mode, which can be started via the "New Game" button. In Scenario Mode, you play as the owner of a mercenary company in a 90s South American setting, taking on multiple assignments. Recruit talented mercenaries, buy weapons, and develop them to fit their roles and characteristics. Observe how your mercenaries perform in battle and plan your tactics to succeed in your missions.

[h1]Future plans[/h1]

A lot more work needs to be done to realize the gameplay experience we envisioned when we first started the project. I'd like to share some of the high-priority things the team would like to do in the future.

[list]
[*] Replayable, or replayable gameplay: In addition to the scenario mode that you can start with a "new game", we're working on gameplay modes that allow you to play the game over and over again and grow your company. We're experimenting with a number of ideas and can't wait to bring them to life.
[*] In-game interactions: We want to allow players to make simple in-game actions that can affect the outcome of battles. We've prototyped a few ideas, but we don't like them enough to include them in the current build.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44572968/0b371570b45cd1962ff1137fd135ac249a60fd70.png[/img]
[/list]

I'll also share some smaller, gameplay experience improvements we're working on.

[list]
[*] Failure of management issues, recognition of failure, and retrying: When playing a game for the first time, it's sometimes hard for players to recognize if they're making good progress or if they've reached a point where they're virtually unable to continue. We want to make the game's failure states clear, so that players can see what bad choices they made (or game systems they didn't consider) that caused the problem, and feel like they can do better if they play the game again.
[*] More interesting routine progression: The training schedule feels pretty interesting at the beginning of the game, but it's not polished enough to make it interesting to play for long periods of time. We want to improve the progression of the schedule from week to week so that it feels more interesting and gives you something to think about.
[*] UI improvements: We've been working on UI improvements, and we realize that the style and flow of the UI throughout the game is not very organized and we want to improve it.
[/list]


We've tried to polish the game in a short amount of time, but even the playtest build still leaves a lot to be desired. Over the next few weeks, we'll be gradually giving access to the build to those who signed up for the playtest. Your feedback on the game will be very helpful to our development. We look forward to your feedback.

Thank you.
